title: Sorting out dates: Supreme Band, own band and the Depression
summary: Allen and the others try to establish when Labat formed his own band relative to his 1921 marriage and the 1929 Depression.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Right in the back. Back behind you, huh? Yeah. And who would be between the piano and the clarinet and guitar? When did banjos get popular here? Ask Harry, you used to play that. Ask Harry, you used to have banjo play on. You're the first one over here? Or they have them before you? Or, Herbert, what's that boy named Herbert, who? Used to play with the Go Get Them Band. I got him. Yeah, that's when you went to the Go Get Them Band, after him. Yeah. I started after Herbert. You remember that Goldman, the kid in the Goldman? Oh, yeah, yeah. With Paul Maurice? Yeah. I don't know his name, but I don't even know who he's talking. Who did Paul Gorman's sister play with? She played with Celestine. Celestine. Celestine, yeah. Mercedes. Mercedes. I know her. Yes. Mercedes Gorman Fields, her name is, last time I saw her. That's right. I don't know what's happened to her. Oh, she was here this summer. Oh, yeah. That's a lot. I haven't seen her in years. She's from over here? Mm-mm. A brotherly kid. I see. So, you stayed with the Supreme Band for a few years there and formed your own band before you got married, huh? That's right. That's right. I imagine you must have played with the Supreme Band a good eight or nine years.
After you got married, I was thinking, when we got married, it wasn't.
We sure were. You had your own band at the same time?

When you were with the Supreme Band, you didn't play with any other then? No. That's the only band out there. Let's see. Now, we've got to get these years straight in here, because you had so many of them. You got me there. Well, what about the time that the Depression came on? Who were you playing with then? When the Depression hit us? What year was that? 1929. That's right. I guess I was with the Supreme Band then. Still with the Supreme. No, I think you were. So you hadn't formed your own band up then? No. I think I was with the ass on that. Huh? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. In 29? That's when you went away just about, huh? Sure. Just about. Sure. You were with the Tisdun. When Mr. Cavoey had great the red? Yeah. You were with the first one he had the band. You were with Tisdun.
Yeah. Sure, because he had a band with me. We used to come here, remember your daddy? He's so great. Oh, man, you had a band then. I can't remember that.

It was difficult, because he was all the talk about over here. Oh, man. Something I found. That's all you could hear about. And you know I had made money with you plenty. You played with him for quite a while. Oh, yeah. Yeah. Long years, huh? Long years is right. Bring back members, huh, Harry?
Yes, ma'am, it does. I made money with me, too. That's right.
